resolved.decision: Python 3.14 Flask services on Cloud Run with Firestore and Cloud Storage
Keep App Engine live while the complete replacement runs on a separate candidate endpoint for comparison and real-client testing
Preserve all nine protobuf RPCs and observed HTTP behavior in place
Keep Card and TRS-IO routes permanently on App Engine
Preserve port 80 without redirect for reviewed native clients
Keep synchronized candidate snapshots inactive until a separate guarded handoff
Require three consecutive fresh zero-difference four-surface reports; no fixed-duration wait
Use one dedicated public us-central1 bucket with CDN disabled initially and Cache-Control no-store; CDN remains an optional measured future improvement
Run the complete replacement beside App Engine, require old-versus-new parity and real-client approval, then make one atomic route switch with immediate rollback available
Use next.retrostore.org for the complete parallel replacement and admin-next.retrostore.org for the replacement admin

Create the candidate load balancer, certificates, next/admin-next DNS records, dedicated public static bucket and IAM, and separate candidate Cloud Run services; do not change retrostore.org or production data authority

pending.proposal: 365 days after final App Engine retirement with manual deletion review
Isolated private admin queue; alternatives are confirmed email or explicit retirement
Keep ten historical non-authorizing profiles, retain the matched administrator, manually review two unmatched legacy administrators
